title: LiteratureExtractionSchema
description: A flat standardized academic schema for extracting literature metadata, methodology, findings, boundaries, and research gaps.

title.description: The complete formal title of the paper.

venue.description: The publication venue, conference, journal, or repository name.

publication_type.description: The genre of the publication (e.g., empirical study, systematic survey, benchmark dataset, system paper, theoretical analysis).

problem_statement.description: The central research question, problem, or phenomenon investigated.

domain.description: The target domain, operational setting, language environment, or subject area.

theoretical_framework.description: Underlying theories, conceptual frameworks, or foundational assumptions, or null if unstated.

methodology.description: The primary approach, algorithmic design, qualitative framework, or analytical method.

datasets.description: Datasets, corpora, participants, or artifacts analyzed, or null if non-empirical.

evaluation.description: Evaluation metrics, benchmark scores, statistical tests, or qualitative evaluation procedures, or null if non-empirical.

key_findings.description: Primary quantitative results, qualitative findings, or theoretical conclusions.

scope_and_delimitations.description: Deliberate boundary choices, parameter constraints, and operational scope set by the authors.

limitations.description: Explicit limitations acknowledged by the authors.

verbatim_excerpt.description: A direct quote from the paper acknowledging the limitation.

summary.description: A concise synthesis of the acknowledged limitations.

generalizability_gap.description: Unexamined populations, untested languages, alternative environments, or differing operational scales not covered.

methodological_gap.description: Measurement constraints, unaddressed variables, missing baseline comparisons, or architectural limitations.

future_work.description: Explicit future research trajectories and open challenges recommended by the authors.
